title: paged-kv: implement soft-pin block allocator and reuse heuristics to reduce fragmentation
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: long-lived KV cache entries and block fragmentation were causing elevated tail latency and increased GPU memory pressure under mixed-sequence workloads. This PR introduces a 'soft pin' block allocation strategy and stronger reuse heuristics for the paged KV block manager to reduce allocation churn and eviction storms. Summary of changes: 1) New soft-pin concept for blocks: blocks can be marked soft-pinned when referenced by in-flight decode contexts; they are excluded from immediate eviction but eligible for reuse by same-owner contexts to avoid duplication. 2) Segregated free lists per size class with compact LRU buckets to improve reuse locality. 3) Eviction ranking that factors in last-access timestamp, owner affinity, and live-kv-count to avoid evicting hot multi-token KV pages. 4) GC/compaction path to coalesce small free fragments when fragmentation exceeds threshold. 5) Runtime knobs: kv.soft_pin_v2 (bool), kv.free_list_threshold (int), kv.compact_fraction (float). Design notes: the soft-pin is a lightweight per-block ref-bit plus ownership tag; ownership is used only as a hint for reuse and does not bypass safety checks. Reuse is conservative: blocks reclaimed for reuse must not have active external pointers. Benchmarks: local microbench (mixed chat + completion load, seq distribution 8-1024) shows 10-14% reduction in p99 token-latency and ~12% throughput improvement on T4-equivalent nodes; memory overhead reduced ~6% due to less duplicated KV pages. Rollout plan: feature gated, canary on 5% of hosted traffic, ramp to 50% after 48h if perf signals stable. Backout: revert kv.soft_pin_v2 or set kv.free_list_threshold high. Related work: follow-ups planned to integrate with continuous batching's slot-aware scheduling to further co-locate reuses. Linear tickets: ENG-2143, ENG-2178. Risks: potential subtle race during concurrent eviction and decoder handoff; mitigated with additional CAS checks and stress tests. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] perf benchmarks, [x] canary script, [x] doc update.
commits: 6 commits: initial allocator refactor; add soft-pin metadata and APIs; implement segregated free lists; eviction ranker and compaction; tests and benchmarks; docs and config knobs.
ci_status: pass (one flaky test rerun: kv-pager-stress, rerun succeeded)
review_comments: Ravi Gupta: Can you explain why we prefer soft-pin over exclusive pin? I'm worried about stalling eviction under bursty load.

Ava Martinez: Soft-pin is intentionally low-friction; it prevents immediate eviction only for active handoffs and still allows reuse for same-owner contexts. We observed exclusive pins increased memory pressure because pages couldn't be reused quickly.
Marta Lopez: Nit: add a test for concurrent reuse where two decoders race to acquire the same reclaimed block.
Ava Martinez: Added block_allocator_unit.cc to cover that exact race and added CAS checks in reclaim path.
Kenji Sato: lgtm for allocator design; please add a metric for 'soft_pin_reuse_hits' to track benefit post-rollout.
Ava Martinez: Added metric kv.soft_pin_reuse_hits and a perf dashboard row in docs/architecture/kv_cache_design.md.
release_notes: Improved paged KV block manager with 'soft-pin' allocation, better reuse heuristics, and compaction to reduce fragmentation; expected p99 token latency improvements and reduced memory duplication. Feature gated behind kv.soft_pin_v2.
notes_for_ops: Canary config provided in scripts/perf/canary_kv_softpin.yaml. Watch metrics: kv.evictions, kv.soft_pin_reuse_hits, kv.compaction_runs, gpu_memory_peak, request_p99_token_latency. Backout: disable kv.soft_pin_v2 and reroute canary traffic.
perf_summary: Local perf: 12% throughput increase under mixed-seq load; p95 improved ~6%, p99 improved 10-14% in T4-like environment. Canary early signal: 8% p99 improvement on 5% traffic after 24h with no increase in evictions.
